sanskrit: sa praviśya purīṃ laṅkāṃ rāmabāṇabhayārditaḥ bhagnadarpas tadā rājā babhūva vyathitendriyaḥ
english: Having entered the city of Laṅkā, tormented by fear of Rāma's arrows, the king was then of broken pride, his senses distraught.

sanskrit: mātaṃga iva siṃhena garuḍeneva pannagaḥ abhibhūto 'bhavad rājā rāghaveṇa mahātmanā
english: As an elephant overwhelmed by a lion, as a serpent overwhelmed by Garuḍa, so the king was overpowered by Rāghava, that great-souled one.

sanskrit: brahmadaṇḍaprakāśānāṃ vidyutsadṛśavarcasām smaran rāghavabāṇānāṃ vivyathe rākṣaseśvaraḥ
english: Recalling Rāghava's arrows — blazing like the rod of Brahmā, brilliant as lightning — the lord of the rākṣasas trembled with anguish.

sanskrit: sa kāñcanamayaṃ divyaṃ āśritya paramāsanam vikprekṣamāṇo rakṣāṃsi rāvaṇo vākyam abravīt
english: Resting on his divine golden throne of the highest order, casting his gaze about at the rākṣasas, Rāvaṇa spoke these words.

sanskrit: sarvaṃ tat khalu me moghaṃ yat taptaṃ paramaṃ tapaḥ yat samāno mahendreṇa mānuṣeṇāsmi nirjitaḥ
english: All that supreme austerity I performed has surely been rendered fruitless, since I, equal to great Indra, have been defeated by a mere human.

sanskrit: idaṃ tad brahmaṇo ghoraṃ vākyaṃ mām abhyupasthitam mānuṣebhyo vijānīhi bhayaṃ tvam iti tat tathā
english: That dreadful word of Brahmā has now come upon me: "Know that danger to you will come from humans" — and so it has come to pass.

sanskrit: devadānavagandharvair yakṣarākṣasapannagaiḥ avadhyatvaṃ mayā prāptaṃ mānuṣebhyo na yācitam
english: Invulnerability from gods, dānavas, gandharvas, yakṣas, rākṣasas, and serpents was obtained by me, but I did not beg it from humans.

sanskrit: etad evābhyupāgamya yatnaṃ kartum ihārhatha rākṣasāś cāpi tiṣṭhantu caryāgopuramūrdhasu
english: Recognising this, you must make effort here; and let the rākṣasas stand guard atop the patrol towers and city gates.

sanskrit: sa cāpratimagambhīro devadānavadarpahā brahmaśāpābhibhūtas tu kumbhakarṇo vibodhyatām
english: And that one of incomparable depth, crusher of the pride of gods and dānavas, yet now overcome by Brahmā's curse — let Kumbhakarṇa be awakened.

sanskrit: sa parājitam ātmānaṃ prahastaṃ ca niṣūditam jñātvā rakṣobalaṃ bhīmam ādideśa mahābalaḥ
english: Knowing himself defeated and Prahasta slain, the mighty one commanded the terrible army of rākṣasas.

sanskrit: dvāreṣu yatnaḥ kriyatāṃ prākārāś cādhiruhyatām nidrāvaśasamāviṣṭaḥ kumbhakarṇo vibodhyatām
english: "Let vigil be kept at the gates, let the ramparts be mounted, and let Kumbhakarṇa, seized by the power of sleep, be awakened."

sanskrit: nava ṣaṭ sapta cāṣṭau ca māsān svapiti rākṣasaḥ taṃ tu bodhayata kṣipraṃ kumbhakarṇaṃ mahābalam
english: "That rākṣasa sleeps for nine, six, seven, or eight months at a stretch — quickly rouse that mighty Kumbhakarṇa now."

sanskrit: sa hi saṃkhye mahābāhuḥ kakudaṃ sarvarakṣasām vānarān rājaputrau ca kṣipram eva vadhiṣyati
english: "For he, the long-armed pinnacle of all rākṣasas, will swiftly slay the monkeys and those two princes in battle."

sanskrit: kumbhakarṇaḥ sadā śete mūḍho grāmyasukhe rataḥ rāmeṇābhinirastasya saṃgrāmo 'smin sudāruṇe
english: "Kumbhakarṇa always sleeps, that dull one addicted to base pleasures — but in this most dreadful battle against one driven back by Rāma —

sanskrit: bhaviṣyati na me śokaḥ kumbhakarṇe vibodhite kiṃ kariṣyāmy ahaṃ tena śakratulyabalena hi
english: "there will be no grief for me once Kumbhakarṇa is awakened. What indeed could I not accomplish with one whose strength equals Indra's?"

sanskrit: īdṛśe vyasane prāpte yo na sāhyāya kalpate te tu tad vacanaṃ śrutvā rākṣasendrasya rākṣasāḥ
english: "One who does not rise to aid when such a calamity has arrived—" Having heard that command of the lord of rākṣasas, those rākṣasas

sanskrit: jagmuḥ paramasaṃbhrāntāḥ kumbhakarṇaniveśanam te rāvaṇasamādiṣṭā māṃsaśoṇitabhojanāḥ
english: departed in great haste to the dwelling of Kumbhakarṇa — those appointed by Rāvaṇa who fed on flesh and blood.

sanskrit: gandhamālyāṃs tathā bhakṣyān ādāya sahasā yayuḥ tāṃ praviśya mahādvārāṃ sarvato yojanāyatām
english: Seizing perfumes, garlands, and food, they quickly went and entered through that great gate extending a full yojana in every direction.

sanskrit: kumbhakarṇaguhāṃ ramyāṃ sarvagandhapravāhinīm pratiṣṭhamānāḥ kṛcchreṇa yatnāt praviviśur guhām
english: Moving onward toward that beautiful cave of Kumbhakarṇa, fragrant with all manner of scents, they entered the cave with great effort and difficulty.

sanskrit: tāṃ praviśya guhāṃ ramyāṃ śubhāṃ kāñcanakuṭṭimām dadṛśur nairṛtavyāghraṃ śayānaṃ bhīmadarśanam
english: Entering that beautiful and auspicious cave with its golden floor, they beheld that tiger among rākṣasas lying there, terrible to behold.

sanskrit: te tu taṃ vikṛtaṃ suptaṃ vikīrṇam iva parvatam kumbhakarṇaṃ mahānidraṃ sahitāḥ pratyabodhayan
english: Together they attempted to wake that grotesquely sleeping Kumbhakarṇa, who lay like a scattered mountain, sunk in deep slumber.

sanskrit: ūrdhvaromāñcitatanuṃ śvasantam iva pannagam trāsayantaṃ mahāśvāsaiḥ śayānaṃ bhīmadarśanam
english: His body with hair erect, breathing like a great serpent, terrifying all with his mighty exhalations — he lay there, dreadful to look upon.

sanskrit: bhīmanāsāpuṭaṃ taṃ tu pātālavipulānanam dadṛśur nairṛtavyāghraṃ kumbhakarṇaṃ mahābalam
english: They beheld that tiger among rākṣasas, the mighty Kumbhakarṇa — with his fearsome nostrils and his mouth as vast as the netherworld.

sanskrit: tataś cakrur mahātmānaḥ kumbhakarṇāgratas tadā māṃsānāṃ merusaṃkāśaṃ rāśiṃ paramatarpaṇam
english: Those great ones then piled before Kumbhakarṇa a heap of flesh resembling Mount Meru — the most gratifying of offerings.

sanskrit: mṛgāṇāṃ mahiṣāṇāṃ ca varāhāṇāṃ ca saṃcayān cakrur nairṛtaśārdūlā rāśimann asya cādbhutam
english: Those tigers among rākṣasas assembled heaps of deer, buffaloes, and boars — a wondrous pile placed before him.

sanskrit: tataḥ śoṇitakumbhāṃś ca madyāni vividhāni ca purastāt kumbhakarṇasya cakrus tridaśaśatravaḥ
english: Then those enemies of the gods placed before Kumbhakarṇa jars of blood and various kinds of wine.

sanskrit: lilipuś ca parārdhyena candanena paraṃtapam divyair ācchādayām āsur mālyair gandhaiḥ sugandhibhiḥ
english: They anointed that scorcher of foes with the finest sandalwood paste and adorned him with divine garlands and sweet-smelling fragrances.

sanskrit: dhūpaṃ sugandhaṃ sasṛjus tuṣṭuvuś ca paraṃtapam jaladā iva conedur yātudhānāḥ sahasraśaḥ
english: They wafted fragrant incense about and praised that scorcher of foes; the yātudhānas roared in their thousands like rain-clouds.

sanskrit: śaṅkhān āpūrayām āsuḥ śaśāṅkasadṛśaprabhān tumulaṃ yugapac cāpi vineduś cāpy amarṣitāḥ
english: They filled conch shells bright as the moon and simultaneously raised a tumultuous clamor, and in their fury they roared all at once.

sanskrit: nedur āsphoṭayām āsuś cikṣipus te niśācarāḥ kumbhakarṇavibodhārthaṃ cakrus te vipulaṃ svanam
english: Those night-roamers shouted, clapped their arms, hurled things about, and made a vast din for the purpose of waking Kumbhakarṇa.

sanskrit: saśaṅkhabherīpaṭahapraṇādam āsphoṭitakṣveḍitasiṃhanādam diśo dravantas tridivaṃ kirantaḥ śrutvā vihaṃgāḥ sahasā nipetuḥ
english: The din of conches, war-drums, and kettledrums, along with clapping, battle-cries, and lion-roars filling all directions and piercing the heavens — hearing it, birds fell suddenly to the ground.

sanskrit: yadā bhṛśaṃ tair ninadair mahātmā na kumbhakarṇo bubudhe prasuptaḥ tato musuṇḍīmusalāni sarve rakṣogaṇās te jagṛhur gadāś ca
english: When even with those great noises the mighty Kumbhakarṇa, deep in slumber, did not awake, then all those companies of rākṣasas seized clubs, pestles, and maces.

sanskrit: taṃ śailaśṛṅgair musalair gadābhir vṛkṣais talair mudgaramuṣṭibhiś ca sukhaprasuptaṃ bhuvi kumbhakarṇaṃ rakṣāṃsy udagrāṇi tadā nijaghnuḥ
english: Those towering rākṣasas then struck Kumbhakarṇa, lying at ease in deep slumber on the ground, with mountain peaks, pestles, maces, trees, palm-blows, sledge-hammers, and fists.

sanskrit: tasya niśvāsavātena kumbhakarṇasya rakṣasaḥ rākṣasā balavanto 'pi sthātuṃ nāśaknuvan puraḥ
english: Even the mighty rākṣasas could not stand before the blast of the breath of that rākṣasa Kumbhakarṇa's exhalations.

sanskrit: tato 'sya purato gāḍhaṃ rākṣasā bhīmavikramāḥ mṛdaṅgapaṇavān bherīḥ śaṅkhakumbhagaṇāṃs tathā daśarākṣasasāhasraṃ yugapat paryavādayan
english: Then those rākṣasas of terrible prowess beat hard before him mṛdaṅgas, paṇavas, war-drums, conches, and kettledrums — ten thousand rākṣasas all sounding them simultaneously.

sanskrit: nīlāñjanacayākāraṃ te tu taṃ pratyabodhayan abhighnanto nadantaś ca naiva saṃvivide tu saḥ
english: They tried to rouse that one who resembled a heap of dark collyrium, striking him and shouting — but he was utterly unaware.

sanskrit: yadā cainaṃ na śekus te pratibodhayituṃ tadā tato gurutaraṃ yatnaṃ dāruṇaṃ samupākraman
english: When they were unable to wake him, they then undertook a more severe and terrible effort.

sanskrit: aśvān uṣṭrān kharān nāgāñ jaghnur daṇḍakaśāṅkuśaiḥ bherīśaṅkhamṛdaṅgāṃś ca sarvaprāṇair avādayan
english: They beat horses, camels, donkeys, and elephants with sticks, whips, and goads, and sounded the war-drums, conches, and mṛdaṅgas with all their might.

sanskrit: nijaghnuś cāsya gātrāṇi mahākāṣṭhakaṭaṃ karaiḥ mudgarair musalaiś caiva sarvaprāṇasamudyataiḥ
english: They struck his limbs with great timbers, logs, sledge-hammers, and pestles, exerting their full strength.

sanskrit: tena śabdena mahatā laṅkā samabhipūritā saparvatavanā sarvā so 'pi naiva prabudhyate
english: With that tremendous noise all of Laṅkā was filled, along with its mountains and forests — yet he still did not awaken.

sanskrit: tataḥ sahasraṃ bherīṇāṃ yugapat samahanyata mṛṣṭakāñcanakoṇānām asaktānāṃ samantataḥ
english: Then a thousand war-drums fitted with polished golden strikers were beaten simultaneously, all around him without pause.

sanskrit: evam apy atinidras tu yadā naiva prabudhyata śāpasya vaśam āpannas tataḥ kruddhā niśācarāḥ
english: Even so, when that one of extreme slumber, fallen under the power of the curse, did not wake, the night-roamers grew angry.

sanskrit: mahākrodhasamāviṣṭāḥ sarve bhīmaparākramāḥ tad rakṣobodhayiṣyantaś cakrur anye parākramam
english: Possessed by great rage, all of them of terrible valor, others again made fresh exertion to rouse that rākṣasa.

sanskrit: anye bherīḥ samājaghnur anye cakrur mahāsvanam keśān anye pralulupuḥ karṇāv anye daśanti ca na kumbhakarṇaḥ paspande mahānidrāvaśaṃ gataḥ
english: Some beat war-drums, others raised a mighty clamor, some pulled at his hair, others bit at his ears — yet Kumbhakarṇa, overcome by deep sleep, did not stir.

sanskrit: anye ca balinas tasya kūṭamudgarapāṇayaḥ mūrdhni vakṣasi gātreṣu pātayan kūṭamudgarān
english: Other strong ones, holding iron sledge-hammers, rained down blows upon his head, chest, and limbs.

sanskrit: rajjubandhanabaddhābhiḥ śataghnībhiś ca sarvataḥ vadhyamāno mahākāyo na prābudhyata rākṣasaḥ
english: Though struck all around with śataghnis bound with rope-ties, that great-bodied rākṣasa did not wake.

sanskrit: vāraṇānāṃ sahasraṃ tu śarīre 'sya pradhāvitam kumbhakarṇas tado buddhaḥ sparśaṃ param abudhyata
english: Then a thousand elephants were driven to run across his body — and only then did Kumbhakarṇa stir, becoming faintly conscious of the touch.

sanskrit: sa pātyamānair giriśṛṅgavṛkṣair acintayaṃs tān vipulān prahārān nidrākṣayāt kṣudbhayapīḍitaś ca vijṛmbhamāṇaḥ sahasotpapāta
english: With mountain peaks and trees being hurled upon him, heeding not those great blows, his sleep at last exhausted, tormented by hunger, he stretched himself yawning and suddenly sprang up.

sanskrit: sa nāgabhogācalaśṛṅgakalpau vikṣipya bāhū giriśṛṅgasārau vivṛtya vaktraṃ vaḍavāmukhābhaṃ niśācaro 'sau vikṛtaṃ jajṛmbhe
english: That night-roamer flung wide his two arms — each like the body of a great serpent or the summit of a mountain — and opening his mouth, which resembled the submarine fire, yawned in a monstrous fashion.

sanskrit: tasya jājṛmbhamāṇasya vaktraṃ pātālasaṃnibham dadṛśe meruśṛṅgāgre divākara ivoditaḥ
english: As he yawned, his mouth resembling the netherworld was seen like the sun risen above the peak of Mount Meru.

sanskrit: vijṛmbhamāṇo 'tibalaḥ pratibuddho niśācaraḥ niśvāsaś cāsya saṃjajñe parvatād iva mārutaḥ
english: That night-roamer of tremendous strength, now awake and stretching, breathed out a breath that arose like wind from a mountain.

sanskrit: rūpam uttiṣṭhatas tasya kumbhakarṇasya tad babhau tapānte sabalākasya meghasyeva vivarṣataḥ
english: The form of Kumbhakarṇa as he rose up shone like a rain-laden cloud, crowded with lightning, pouring down rain at the end of summer.

sanskrit: tasya dīptāgnisadṛśe vidyutsadṛśavarcasī dadṛśāte mahānetre dīptāv iva mahāgrahau
english: His two great eyes, blazing like fierce fire, brilliant as lightning, were seen like two great planets burning bright.

sanskrit: ādad bubhukṣito māṃsaṃ śoṇitaṃ tṛṣito 'pibat medaḥ kumbhaṃ ca madyaṃ ca papau śakraripus tadā
english: Hungry, he devoured the flesh; thirsty, he drank blood; and that enemy of Indra then drank from jars of fat and wine.

sanskrit: tatas tṛpta iti jñātvā samutpetur niśācarāḥ śirobhiś ca praṇamyainaṃ sarvataḥ paryavārayan
english: Then, knowing him satiated, the night-roamers arose and, bowing their heads in reverence, surrounded him on all sides.

sanskrit: sa sarvān sāntvayām āsa nairṛtān nairṛtarṣabhaḥ bodhanād vismitaś cāpi rākṣasān idam abravīt
english: That bull among rākṣasas consoled all the rākṣasas, and being also astonished at being awakened, spoke these words to the rākṣasas.

sanskrit: kimartham aham āhatya bhavadbhiḥ pratibodhitaḥ kaccit sukuśalaṃ rājño bhayaṃ vā neha kiṃ cana
english: "For what reason have you beaten and awakened me? Is the king in good health? Is there no danger anywhere here?"

sanskrit: atha vā dhruvam anyebhyo bhayaṃ param upasthitam yadartham eva tvaritair bhavadbhiḥ pratibodhitaḥ
english: "Or has some great danger surely arisen from others — for which reason you have awakened me in such haste?"

sanskrit: adya rākṣasarājasya bhayam utpāṭayāmy aham pātayiṣye mahendraṃ vā śātayiṣye tathānalam
english: "This very day I shall root out the danger of the lord of rākṣasas — I shall strike down great Indra or I shall extinguish Agni himself."

sanskrit: na hy alpakāraṇe suptaṃ bodhayiṣyati māṃ bhṛśam tad ākhyātārthatattvena matprabodhanakāraṇam
english: "For no trifling reason would you wake me so forcefully in my sleep. Therefore, tell me truly the cause for my awakening."

sanskrit: evaṃ bruvāṇaṃ saṃrabdhaṃ kumbhakarṇam ariṃdamam yūpākṣaḥ sacivo rājñaḥ kṛtāñjalir uvāca ha
english: To Kumbhakarṇa, that subduer of enemies, speaking thus in agitation, Yūpākṣa, minister of the king, spoke with joined palms.

sanskrit: na no devakṛtaṃ kiṃ cid bhayam asti kadā cana na daityadānavebhyo vā bhayam asti hi tādṛśam yādṛśaṃ mānuṣaṃ rājan bhayam asmān upasthitam
english: "No danger to us has ever come from the gods, nor is there any such danger from daityas or dānavas — as the human danger, O king, that has now come upon us."

sanskrit: vānaraiḥ parvatākārair laṅkeyaṃ parivāritā sītāharaṇasaṃtaptād rāmān nas tumulaṃ bhayam
english: "This Laṅkā is surrounded by mountain-like monkeys; a tumultuous danger to us comes from Rāma, who is burning with grief over the abduction of Sītā."

sanskrit: ekena vānareṇeyaṃ pūrvaṃ dagdhā mahāpurī kumāro nihataś cākṣaḥ sānuyātraḥ sakuñjaraḥ
english: "This great city was previously burned by a single monkey; Prince Akṣa was slain along with his retinue and his elephant."

sanskrit: svayaṃ rakṣo'dhipaś cāpi paulastyo devakaṇṭakaḥ mṛteti saṃyuge muktārāmeṇādityatejasā
english: "And the lord of rākṣasas himself, descendant of Pulastya, thorn in the side of the gods, was left for dead in battle when Rāma, blazing like the sun, released him."

sanskrit: yan na devaiḥ kṛto rājā nāpi daityair na dānavaiḥ kṛtaḥ sa iha rāmeṇa vimuktaḥ prāṇasaṃśayāt
english: "He whom neither the gods, daityas, nor dānavas could reduce to such a state — he was here released by Rāma from peril to his very life."

sanskrit: sa yūpākṣavacaḥ śrutvā bhrātur yudhi parājayam kumbhakarṇo vivṛttākṣo yūpākṣam idam abravīt
english: Having heard Yūpākṣa's words about his brother's defeat in battle, Kumbhakarṇa, with rolling eyes, spoke thus to Yūpākṣa.

sanskrit: sarvam adyaiva yūpākṣa harisainyaṃ salakṣmaṇam rāghavaṃ ca raṇe hatvā paścād drakṣyāmi rāvaṇam
english: "This very day, O Yūpākṣa, I shall slay the monkey army along with Lakṣmaṇa and Rāghava in battle — and after that I shall go to see Rāvaṇa."

sanskrit: rākṣasāṃs tarpayiṣyāmi harīṇāṃ māṃsaśoṇitaiḥ rāmalakṣmaṇayoś cāpi svayaṃ pāsyāmi śoṇitam
english: "I shall satisfy the rākṣasas with the flesh and blood of the monkeys, and I myself shall drink the blood of Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa."

sanskrit: tat tasya vākyaṃ bruvato niśamya sagarvitaṃ roṣavivṛddhadoṣam mahodaro nairṛtayodhamukhyaḥ kṛtāñjalir vākyam idaṃ babhāṣe
english: Hearing those proud words of his, whose fault was the swelling of wrath, Mahodara, foremost warrior among the rākṣasas, spoke these words with joined palms.

sanskrit: rāvaṇasya vacaḥ śrutvā guṇadoṣu vimṛśya ca paścād api mahābāho śatrūn yudhi vijeṣyasi
english: "Having heard Rāvaṇa's words and deliberated on merits and faults, you may thereafter conquer the enemies in battle, O long-armed one."

sanskrit: mahodaravacaḥ śrutvā rākṣasaiḥ parivāritaḥ kumbhakarṇo mahātejāḥ saṃpratasthe mahābalaḥ
english: Having heard Mahodara's words, Kumbhakarṇa of great brilliance, the mighty one, surrounded by rākṣasas, set out.

sanskrit: taṃ samutthāpya bhīmākṣaṃ bhīmarūpaparākramam rākṣasās tvaritā jagmur daśagrīvaniveśanam
english: Having roused him of terrible eyes and terrifying form and valor, the rākṣasas hastened to the dwelling of the ten-necked Rāvaṇa.

sanskrit: tato gatvā daśagrīvam āsīnaṃ paramāsane ūcur baddhāñjalipuṭāḥ sarva eva niśācarāḥ
english: Then, going to the ten-necked one seated on his supreme throne, all the night-roamers with folded palms spoke.

sanskrit: prabuddhaḥ kumbhakarṇo 'sau bhrātā te rākṣasarṣabha kathaṃ tatraiva niryātu drakṣyase tam ihāgatam
english: "Kumbhakarṇa your brother is awakened, O bull among rākṣasas. Please let him come forth from there — or you will see him arrived here."

sanskrit: rāvaṇas tv abravīd dhṛṣṭo yathānyāyaṃ ca pūjitam draṣṭum enam ihecchāmi yathānyāyaṃ ca pūjitam
english: Rāvaṇa then said, delighted: "I wish to see him here, duly honored — let him be received with fitting honor."

sanskrit: tathety uktvā tu te sarve punar āgamya rākṣasāḥ kumbhakarṇam idaṃ vākyam ūcū rāvaṇacoditāḥ
english: Saying "So be it," all those rākṣasas returned and, urged by Rāvaṇa, spoke these words to Kumbhakarṇa.

sanskrit: draṣṭuṃ tvāṃ kāṅkṣate rājā sarvarākṣasapuṃgavaḥ gamane kriyatāṃ buddhir bhrātaraṃ saṃpraharṣaya
english: "The king, foremost of all rākṣasas, desires to see you — resolve to go and gladden your brother."

sanskrit: kumbhakarṇas tu durdharṣo bhrātur ājñāya śāsanam tathety uktvā mahāvīryaḥ śayanād utpapāta ha
english: Kumbhakarṇa, that irresistible one, accepting his brother's command, said "So be it," and that mighty one sprang up from his bed.

sanskrit: prakṣālya vadanaṃ hṛṣṭaḥ snātaḥ paramabhūṣitaḥ pipāsus tvarayām āsa pānaṃ balasamīraṇam
english: Washing his face, joyful, having bathed and adorned himself with the finest ornaments, thirsty, he urgently called for drink that would restore his strength.

sanskrit: tatas te tvaritās tasya rājaśasā rāvaṇājñayā madyaṃ bhakṣyāṃś ca vividhān kṣipram evopahārayan
english: Then those rākṣasas, acting swiftly and at Rāvaṇa's command, quickly brought him wine and all manner of food.

sanskrit: pītvā ghaṭasahasraṃ sa gamanāyopacakrame
english: Having drunk a thousand jars, he made ready to depart.

sanskrit: īṣatsamutkaṭo mattas tejobalasamanvitaḥ kumbhakarṇo babhau hṛṣṭaḥ kālāntakayamopamaḥ
english: Slightly intoxicated, exhilarated, endowed with blazing energy and strength, Kumbhakarṇa shone joyfully, resembling Yama at the end of a cosmic age.

sanskrit: bhrātuḥ sa bhavanaṃ gacchan rakṣobalasamanvitaḥ kumbhakarṇaḥ padanyāsair akampayata medinīm
english: As Kumbhakarṇa went to his brother's palace, accompanied by the rākṣasa forces, his footfalls made the earth tremble.

sanskrit: sa rājamārgaṃ vapuṣā prakāśayan sahasraraśmir dharaṇīm ivāṃśubhiḥ jagāma tatrāñjalimālayā vṛtaḥ śatakratur geham iva svayambhuvaḥ
english: Illuminating the royal road with his form as the sun with a thousand rays illumines the earth, he went there surrounded by garlands of joined-palm salutations — as Indra goes to the house of Svayambhū.

sanskrit: ke cic charaṇyaṃ śaraṇaṃ sma rāmaṃ vrajanti ke cid vyathitāḥ patanti ke cid diśaḥ sma vyathitāḥ prayānti ke cid bhayārtā bhuvi śerate sma
english: Some, distressed, sought refuge in Rāma the refuge; others fell overwhelmed; others, overcome, fled in all directions; others, stricken with fear, lay prostrate on the ground.

sanskrit: tam adriśṛṅgapratimaṃ kirīṭinaṃ spṛśantam ādityam ivātmatejasā vanaukasaḥ prekṣya vivṛddham adbhutaṃ bhayārditā dudruvire tatas tataḥ
english: The forest-dwellers, seeing that one resembling a mountain peak, crowned and touching the sun as it were with his own blazing splendor, that wondrous giant, fled this way and that, tormented by fear.
